Journal.Title: Wounds : a compendium of clinical research and practice

Article.ArticleTitle: Application of a Skin Adhesive to Maintain Seal in Negative Pressure Wound Therapy: Demonstration of a New Technique.

Abstract.AbstractText: Optimal wound healing with negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) relies on a properly sealed vacuum system. Anatomically difficult wounds impair the adhesive dressing, which results in air leaks that disrupt the integrity of the NPWT system and hinder wound healing.
The authors demonstrate a new technique using a cyanoacrylate-based tissue adhesive to maintain an airtight, durable seal in NPWT.

A 52-year-old woman with a degloving injury to the right thigh extending into the groin, resulting in massive necrosis, presented to the emergency department. Using a skin closure system, 2 polyester mesh tape strips were placed near the perineal region of the wound to reinforce the adhesive drape of the NPWT system. Skin grafts were applied over the wound after about 3 weeks of NPWT, and the skin closure system was applied in the same fashion to reinforce the adhesive drape.

An airtight seal was consistently maintained for several days in between dressing changes. The size of the wound was visibly reduced at each dressing change. An airtight seal was maintained for 5 days after placement of the skin grafts; after 5 days, the dressing was removed without difficulty and skin irritation. The skin grafts appeared healthy with adequate tissue take.

Maintaining an airtight seal in NPWT is crucial to wound healing. Cyanoacrylate tissue adhesives appear to be a safe and viable option for creating a durable seal in NPWT for wounds in anatomically difficult locations.
